c.tagline: Highland capital of red-brick hills, rice paddies and royal history.

taxi.fareNote: Meters are rare; agree on a price before departure or ask your hotel for the going rate.

emergency.note: Tourist police and hotel front desks are the most reliable first contact; response times can be slow.

avoid.reason: Petty crime and banditry — caution in the lower town and at night; don’t display valuables

hood_desc: Historic royal hill with cobblestone lanes, the Rova palace, colonial-era architecture and sweeping city views; quiet at night and best for culture lovers who don't mind steep walks.
Central, walkable district packed with restaurants, bars, art galleries and boutique guesthouses just below Haute-Ville; best for first-time visitors who want charm and easy access to sights on foot.
The bustling commercial heart around the Analakely market and train station, full of budget hotels and street life; best for budget travelers and those prioritizing transit convenience over quiet.
Leafy, modern suburb favored by expats, embassies and NGOs, with newer hotels and a calmer, greener feel; best for business travelers and families wanting safety and comfort over central location.

Riverside business and residential district along the Ankorondrano/Andraharo corridor near international chain hotels and offices; best for business travelers and those wanting modern amenities close to the airport road.

water.note: Microbial contamination risk means tap water should be boiled or avoided; use bottled water instead.

transit.pay: Fares on taxi-be minibuses are paid in cash directly to the conductor (fara-be) upon boarding or alighting, usually a flat fare per route regardless of distance. There is no rechargeable transit card; small Ariary bills/coins are needed as exact change is often expected.
transit.hours: Taxi-be generally run roughly 5:30am-8:30pm with sparse service after dark; there is no formal night transit, so taxis or ride apps are used at night.
transit.note: Routes are numbered and can be crowded and hard for visitors to navigate; taxis and ride-hailing apps are far more practical for tourists than the minibus network.

bus: Long-distance taxi-brousse bush taxis to other regions

transit.m: Taxi-be (shared minibus) to city center, ~45-60 min

tip.r: Not institutionalized or mandatory; around 10% at restaurants and small amounts (a few thousand Ariary) for guides, drivers and porters are appreciated for good service.

food.name: Romazava
food.desc: Madagascar's national dish: a clear ginger-scented beef broth simmered with bitter greens like anamalaho, served over mountains of rice.

places.name: La Varangue
places.note: Colonial villa full of antiques; the city's best-known kitchen for classic Malagasy plates.

places.name: Grand Cafe de la Gare

places.name: Sakamanga

food.name: Ravitoto sy henakisoa
food.desc: Pounded cassava leaves stewed slowly with fatty pork, often finished with coconut milk. Rich, green and deeply savoury.

places.name: La Varangue
places.note: Serves the pork-and-cassava-leaf version alongside romazava and vary amin anana.

places.name: Chez Mariette

places.name: Sakamanga

places.name: Marche d Andravoahangy
places.note: Handmade koba and other Malagasy sweets sold alongside crafts and produce.

food.desc: Chicken braised with coconut milk, ginger and tomato, a coastal favourite that has become a staple on capital menus.

places.name: Sakamanga
places.note: Coconut chicken is a house standard in this decades-old dining room.

places.name: La Varangue

places.name: Chez Mariette

food.name: Ranon ampango
food.desc: The national table drink: water boiled with the toasted rice crust left in the pot, smoky, faintly sweet and served warm with meals.

landmarks: Rova of Antananarivo (Royal Palace)
The hilltop royal palace complex that once housed Madagascar's monarchy, offering sweeping panoramic views over the capital.
Andafiavaratra Palace
A stately 19th-century prime minister's palace turned museum, showcasing royal Merina treasures near the Rova.
Lake Anosy and the Monument aux Morts
A tranquil artificial lake ringed by jacaranda trees with a striking war memorial obelisk reflected in its waters.
Analakely Market (Zoma area)
The bustling downtown market district where colorful stalls and steep stairways capture the everyday rhythm of Tana life.
Ambohimanga (Royal Hill)
A UNESCO World Heritage sacred royal hill just outside the city, considered the spiritual heart of Malagasy identity.
Antananarivo Cathedral (Andohalo Cathedral)
A grand twin-spired cathedral perched on a hillside, blending French colonial architecture with sweeping city vistas.
Andohalo Square
A historic public square where Malagasy sovereigns once addressed their people, still lined with fine colonial-era buildings.
Tsimbazaza Zoo and Botanical Garden
A green oasis showcasing Madagascar's unique lemurs and endemic flora right within the capital.
Haute Ville (Upper Town) Steps and Streets
Steep cobblestone staircases winding past red-brick colonial houses, offering some of the most photogenic street scenes in Tana.
Independence Avenue (Avenue de l'Indépendance)
The grand central boulevard lined with jacaranda trees, colonial architecture, and lively markets in the heart of the city.

train.note: Madagascar is an island, so there is no international rail. Madarail runs a passenger train between Antananarivo (Soarano station) and Antsirabe, reopened in December 2023, plus a short Antananarivo-Ambohimanambola suburban service from December 2025; frequencies are limited and irregular. The scenic Fianarantsoa-Manakara (FCE) line is in the south and cannot be reached by rail from the capital. Note: Madarail's site is http-only.

bus.note: As an island there are no international buses. Long-distance domestic coaches (taxi-brousse) leave Antananarivo's Maki (Ambodivona/Fasan'ny Karana) stations. A major operator with online booking is Cotisse Transport (https://www.cotisse-transport.com/), serving Toamasina, Antsirabe, Mahajanga, Fianarantsoa and more.

ferry.note: No scheduled international passenger ferries from Madagascar. The main seaport, Toamasina (Tamatave), is about 370 km east; only irregular cargo boats link Madagascar with the Comoros and Mayotte.

half.name: Antsirabe
half.blurb: Highland town known for thermal springs, colonial architecture, and rickshaw transport.

full.name: Toamasina
full.blurb: Madagascar's largest port city known for its harbor, beaches, and lively markets.
